**1 — Scene:** A breakfast tray with two fried eggs, two slices of toast, muesli, yogurt, orange juice, milk, and two small spread packets. I treat the items on the tray as one meal.

**2 — Vessels:** Main plate approximately **26 cm** across: area **531 cm²**. Muesli bowl approximately **16 cm**: area **201 cm²**. Drink and yogurt quantities are estimated from their containers and visible fill levels.

**3–6 — Items, coverage, volume, and weight:** Coverage percentages refer to each item’s own vessel. Toast is treated as porous loaf bread, using **0.30 g/ml**.

| Item | Vessel coverage | Area × average height = gross volume | Density → weight |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Two toast slices | 40% of plate | 212 cm² × 1.1 cm = 233 ml | 0.30 → **70 g** |
| Two eggs | 30% of plate | 159 cm² × 0.65 cm = 103 ml | 1.0 → **103 g** |
| Muesli | 35% of bowl | 70 cm² × 1.5 cm = 105 ml | 0.40 → **42 g** |
| Orange juice | Full glass cross-section | 44 cm² × 4.8 cm = 211 ml | 1.04 → **220 g** |
| Milk | Full bottle cross-section | 24 cm² × 4 cm = 96 ml | 1.03 → **99 g** |
| Yogurt | Full cup cross-section | 38 cm² × 3.7 cm = 141 ml | 1.03 → **145 g** |
| Two spread portions | Contents concealed | Approximately 14 ml combined | 0.95 → **13 g** |

The main plate is approximately **70% covered**, consistent with the visible empty rim. The spread and yogurt estimates are less certain because their containers are sealed. No separate quantity of cooking oil is visibly measurable.

**7 — Energy:** Using approximate energy densities for toast, fried eggs as served, dry muesli, juice, milk, Greek-style yogurt, and butter-like spread gives **about 880 kcal**.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **792 g including drinks**, or **473 g excluding juice and milk**, is plausible for this tray. The main plate itself contains approximately **173 g** of eggs and toast.
